evidence: src/infrastructure/persistence/InMemoryOrderRepository.ts: class InMemoryOrderRepository implements OrderRepository with a private readonly orders = new Map<string, Order>() and the methods findById, findByStatus, save and nextId

src/infrastructure/persistence/InMemoryProductRepository.ts: class InMemoryProductRepository implements ProductRepository with a private readonly products = new Map<string, Product>() and the methods findById, findAll and save

src/infrastructure/persistence/seedCatalogue.ts: seedCatalogue(products: ProductRepository) calls products.save(Product.create(...)), so it goes through the repository abstraction and the domain factory rather than the Map
Id generation (randomUUID in nextId) appears only in InMemoryOrderRepository; no invariant is duplicated across the files
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All three files deal with one concern: in-memory persistence for the domain's repositories. InMemoryOrderRepository and InMemoryProductRepository implement the domain repository interfaces the same way, each keeping a private Map keyed by entity id. seedCatalogue loads initial data through the ProductRepository abstraction and builds entities with the domain factory Product.create. It does not reach into the in-memory Map directly, so no abstraction is bypassed. The two repositories share a similar Map pattern, but that is plain storage code, not a duplicated business rule or invariant. Id generation (nextId) lives only in the order repository. No file belongs to an unrelated concern.
